scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The cordax originated as a buffoonish dance of Lydian origin, later becoming a permanent fixture of ancient Attic comedy and private symposia.
It persisted through Roman literature via writers like Juvenal and Petronius, and continued to be referenced in medieval texts by Rabelais and others.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Associated with drunkenness, comic relief, and theatrical satire, the dance also held a sacred dimension, being dedicated to the goddess Artemis in Elis following a military victory.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involved particular turns, staggers, and vulgar body movements.
Dancers engaged in lively, brio-filled steps that culminated in sinking to the ground with tremulous buttocks amid audience applause.
Watch for Tremulous sinking.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The musical accompaniment relied on percussion and wind instruments, specifically the clicking of castanets, finger cymbals, flutes, hand drums, and harps, forming a bouncing trochaic rhythm.
Listen for the flutes, hand drums, harps, castanets.
The pulse is trochaic.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performers wore theatrical masks and, in comedic contexts, oversized, red, erect artificial penises.
It was performed on theatrical comedy stages and during the symposion phase of banquets.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Aristophanes, Petronius, Juvenal, Trimalchio, Fortunata, Theophrastus, Pausanias, and Karl August Böttiger.
Transitioned from Lydian roots to ancient Greek comedy, Roman adaptations, and later theoretical links to European folk forms like the tarantella and fandango.
Linked by theorists to ancient Greek comedy, the worship of Artemis in Elis, and proposed as an ancient predecessor to modern belly dance, tsifteteli, fandango, and tarantella.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: cordax is variant of tsifteteli: Theorized modern Greek descendant of the ancient cordax.
cordax is sibling of komos: Ancient Greek ritual revelry associated with drunkenness and dance.
cordax is influence of fandango: Suggested by scholars as a modern descendant due to castanet accompaniment.
